judgment: Crossing the courtyard, no one seen.
image: lets no thought leave its place.
lines: What it follows, it cannot lift.
splitting the muscles of the back.

notes.name_en: 艮 is used as a verb throughout ('still the toes/waist/jaws') and as the mountain trigram only in the Image （兼山）. Title takes the verb ('Stilling'), rejecting 'Stillness' (abstraction) and Wilhelm's 'Keeping Still, Mountain'.
notes.judgment: 艮其背不獲其身行其庭不見其人無咎。 The back is the part that cannot see or grab: stilling there, the body is 'not caught' （獲 kept as catch/get hold of) and courtyard people go unseen. Kept literal against Legge's paraphrase 'loses all consciousness of self'. Possessive 其 dropped throughout per style (no 'his').
notes.image: 兼山艮；君子以思不出其位。 兼 = doubled/joined mountains. 位 kept spatial as 'place' (position in the world), not narrowed to duties or office.
notes.L2: 六二 艮其腓不拯其隨其心不快。 Subject of 隨 is ambiguous — calf following thigh, or this line following the one above. 'What it follows, it cannot lift' keeps the ambiguity; 拯 = lift up/rescue, rendered with its physical verb 'lift'. 快 = glad.
notes.L3: 九三 艮其限列其夤厲薰心。 限 is the waist as a threshold/boundary between lower and upper body; 夤 are the muscles along the spine, split （列） when stilling is forced at the join. 薰 kept as a verb: danger smokes/fumes the heart.
notes.L4: 六四 艮其身。 身 narrowed to 'trunk' by the ascending sequence toes → calves → waist → trunk → jaws; in the Judgment 身 is the whole body.
notes.L5: 六五 艮其輔言有序悔亡。 輔 are the cheek/jaw bones that move in speech — 'jaws'. 悔亡 per glossary, distinct from 無悔.
notes.L6: 上九 敦艮吉。 敦 is thick, solid, substantial — 'made solid', not Legge's moralised 'devotedly maintaining'.
